title: Chapter 4: Globalization and Regionalism
content:
👋 ሰላም የተወደዳችሁ የ-EthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! እንኳን ወደ Global Trends and International Relations የምዕራፍ 4 የመጨረሻው ክፍል ቱቶሪያል በሰላም መጣችሁ። በዚህ ክፍል ከ 4.7 እስከ ምዕራፋ መጨረሻ ያለውን ፅንሰ-ሀሳብ እንዳስሳለን፤ በብርታት ተከታተሉን

4.7. Major Theories of Regional Integrations

4.7.1. Functionalism

Functionalist viewed regionalism as a functional response by states to the problems that derived from regional interdependence. It was seen as the most effective means of solving common problems. Regionalism has started from technical and non-controversial issues and has spilled over into the realm of high politics and redefinition of group identity around the regional unit (Hurrell 1995). According to functionalism, the task of policy makers is to encourage the states to peacefully work together. The like-minded states would spread the web of international activities and agencies in which and through which the interests and life of all states would be gradually integrated from one activity to others (Mitrany 1946).

Regional organization was then built up to cope with one common problem and spill over to other problems and areas of cooperation, which will deepen integration among member states. Therefore, 'spillover' is the key explanation of functionalist regionalism. According to Hurrell (1995), there were two sorts of spillover: First, functional spillover whereby cooperation in one area would broaden and deepen further areas; and second, political spillover whereby the existence of supranational institutions would set in motion a self-reinforcing process of institution building. The end-result would be a shift in loyalties from nationalism towards regionalism. Karns and Mingst (2005) argue that functionalism is applicable at both regional and global levels, noting that overwhelming numbers of IGOs (International Governmental Organizations) have specific mandates, link to economic issues, and have limited memberships.

👉 ፋንክሽናሊዝም (Functionalism) ማለት ሀገራት በጋራ የሚያጋጥሟቸውን የጋራ ችግሮች ለመፍታት ሲሉ በትንንሽ እና ፖለቲካዊ ባልሆኑ (Technical/Non-controversial) ጉዳዮች ላይ የሚያደርጉት ትብብር ነው። ይህ ትብብር እያደገ ሲሄድ ወደ ትላልቅ የፖለቲካ ጉዳዮች (High politics) ይሸጋገራል። የዚህ ቲዮሪ ዋና ቁልፍ ቃል 'Spillover' (መፍሰስ/መዛመት) ነው። ምሳሌ፦ ኢትዮጵያ እና ጅቡቲ መጀመሪያ የጀመሩት በወደብ አጠቃቀም እና በባቡር መስመር ዝርጋታ (Technical/Economic issue) ነበር። ይህ ግንኙነት እያደገ መጥቶ አሁን ወደ ከፍተኛ የፖለቲካ እና የጸጥታ ትብብር (Spillover) አድጓል። ዜጎችም ከብሄራዊ ስሜት ይልቅ ቀጠናዊ ስሜት (Regionalism) እንዲሰማቸው ያደርጋል።

😅 EthioFresh Humor Break: የ "Spillover effect" ነገር ልክ ግቢ ውስጥ "አሳይመንት አብረን እንስራ" ብላችሁ ተገናኝታችሁ፣ ከዛ ወደ "ሻይ አብረን እንጠጣ" አድጎ፣ መጨረሻ ላይ ሪሌሺንሺፕ (Relationship) ውስጥ እንደመግባት ነው! ጀመራችሁት አካዳሚክ (Functional)፣ ጨረሳችሁት ፖለቲካ/ፍቅር (High Politics)! አያችሁት አይደል መዛመቱን (Spillover)? 😂

4.7.2. Neo-functionalism

Neo-functionalism emerged in the 1960s based on the key works of Ernst Haas and Leon Lindberg. The model of integration is based on the following basic principles. Neo-functionalism included clear departures from transactionalism, federalism and functionalism, which made it clearly a distinct and independent theoretical entity. Transactionalism had defined integration as a condition, measured by a 'security-community'. Neo-functionalists, on the contrary, defined integration as a process. Haas (1968) defined it as the process whereby political actors in several distinct national settings are persuaded to shift their loyalties, expectations and political activities towards a new centre.

Another distinguishing principle of neo-functionalism is the emphasis on political agency in the integration process. According to Lindberg, there are preconditions for the success of an integration process:
1) Central institutions and central policies should be established and developed to solve disputes.
2) Their tasks and capacity should go well beyond the mandate of normal international institutions.
3) Their tasks should be inherently expansive.
4) There should be some link between the interests of member states and the process of integration.

👉 ኒዮ-ፋንክሽናሊዝም (Neo-functionalism) ከድሮው ፋንክሽናሊዝም ትንሽ ከፍ ያለ ነው። ይሄኛው ኢንቴግሬሽንን (ውህደትን) እንደ 'ሂደት' (Process) ነው የሚያየው እንጂ እንደ 'ሁኔታ' አያየውም። ዋናው ሀሳባቸው ፖለቲካዊ ተቋማት እና የፖለቲካ ተዋናዮች (Political agency) በውህደቱ ውስጥ ትልቅ ሚና አላቸው የሚል ነው። ሊንድበርግ (Lindberg) እንደሚለው፣ ውህደት እንዲሳካ ጠንካራ ማዕከላዊ ተቋማት (Central institutions) ሊኖሩ ይገባል። ምሳሌ፦ የአውሮፓ ህብረት (EU) ጠንካራ ማዕከላዊ ፓርላማ እና ፍርድ ቤት አለው። አባል ሀገራቱ ስልጣናቸውን ለዚህ ማዕከላዊ አካል አሳልፈው ይሰጣሉ (Shift of loyalties)።

💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ የ Transactionalism እና የ Neo-functionalism ልዩነት ይወጣል። Transactionalism ውህደትን እንደ 'Condition' (ሁኔታ) ሲያየው፣ Neo-functionalism ግን እንደ 'Process' (ሂደት) ነው የሚያየው ብላችሁ መልሱ። እንዲሁም የ 'Spillover' ፅንሰ-ሀሳብን መጀመሪያ ያመጣው (coined by) Ernst Haas መሆኑን አትዘንጉ!

Inter-governmentalism

Inter-governmentalism or liberal intergovernmentalism is a theory and approach that focus on the state for integration to succeed. It approaches the question of the state in an integration process from the perspective of traditional international relations. It considers the state mainly as an actor in the international system. According to Moravcsik (1993), integration can be considered as part of the rational choice of state actors. This rationalist framework disaggregates the process of integration into three stages: national preference formation, interstate bargaining, and institutional choice. National governments may pursue international agendas to satisfy domestic producer groups, subject to geopolitical interests and ideological commitments.

👉 ኢንተር-ገቨርመንታሊዝም (Inter-governmentalism) ዋና ትኩረቱን የሚያደርገው 'ሀገር' (State) ላይ ነው። አንድ ውህደት ሊሳካ የሚችለው ሀገራት (States) በራሳቸው ፍላጎት እና ስሌት (Rational choice) ሲወስኑ ብቻ ነው ይላል። እያንዳንዱ ሀገር ወደ ውህደት የሚገባው የራሱን ሀገራዊ ጥቅም (National preference) ለማስከበር ነው። ምሳሌ፦ በኢጋድ (IGAD) ውስጥ ያሉ ሀገራት (እንደ ኢትዮጵያ፣ ኬንያ፣ ዩጋንዳ) የሚሰባሰቡት የየራሳቸውን ሀገራዊ የፀጥታ እና የኢኮኖሚ ጥቅም ለማስጠበቅ በሚያደርጉት ድርድር (Interstate bargaining) ነው። ገቢቶ?

Supra-nationalism

In order to understand the supranational perception of European integration, we must first study Neo-functionalism. The roots lie visibly in the works of Haas (1958). He developed three mechanisms through which European integration progresses: first, positive spillover effects; second, a transfer of allegiances from the national to the supranational political arena; and third, a 'technocratic automaticity,' referring to an increasingly autonomous role of supranational institutions in promoting further integration. Haas first sees integration as a process led by elitist groups, like leaders of industry associations or political parties, who push national governments to transfer policy competence to a supranational body.

👉 ሱፕራ-ናሽናሊዝም (Supra-nationalism) ማለት ከሀገር በላይ የሆነ (Above the nation-state) ስልጣን ያለው ተቋም መፍጠር ማለት ነው። ሀገራት የራሳቸውን ሉዓላዊነት (Sovereignty) ቀንሰው ለጋራ ትልቅ ተቋም ስልጣን ይሰጣሉ። ይህ ሂደት በሊሂቃን (Elitist groups) የሚመራ ነው። ምሳሌ፦ የአውሮፓ ኮሚሽን (European Commission) ከማንኛውም አባል ሀገር በላይ ሆኖ ህግ ሊያወጣ እና ውሳኔ ሊያሳልፍ ይችላል። የአፍሪካ ህብረትም (AU) ወደ ሱፕራ-ናሽናል ደረጃ ለማደግ ራዕይ አለው፣ ግን ገና አላደረገውም።

4.8. Selected Cases of Regional Integration

Regional integration across the world followed divergent trajectories but was mainly influenced by the development in Europe. Therefore, the idea of regional integration is Eurocentric. Three cases discussed are the European Union (EU), Association of South East Asian States (ASEAN), and African Union (AU).

The European Union (EU): Began as the European Economic Community, underwent changes creating a common market, currency, and institutional harmonization to become a consolidated regional organization.
The African Union (AU): Evolved from the Organization of African Unity (OAU), which expired after ensuring decolonization of African countries. The AU (established in 2002) imitated the EU to realize the unification of African markets towards eventual political unification (creating African Free Trade Areas, visa on arrival, etc.).
ASEAN: Founded in 1967. The region was shaped by nationalism, decolonization, and great power intervention. The main motive initially was not economic but political/security. After the 1997 economic crisis, the region advanced economic goals (APFTA in 1992).

👉 እዚህ ጋር ሶስት ታላላቅ የውህደት ምሳሌዎችን እናያለን።
1. EU (አውሮፓ ህብረት)፦ የሁሉም ውህደቶች አባት እና ሞዴል (Eurocentric) ነው። የጋራ ገበያ እና የጋራ ገንዘብ (ዩሮ) ፈጥረዋል።
2. AU (አፍሪካ ህብረት)፦ ቀድሞ OAU (የአፍሪካ አንድነት ድርጅት) ይባል ነበር፤ አላማውም አፍሪካን ከቅኝ ግዛት ነፃ ማውጣት ነበር። በ2002 ወደ AU ሲቀየር ግን አላማው ወደ ኢኮኖሚ እና ፖለቲካ ውህደት አደገ። የአፍሪካ ነፃ የንግድ ቀጠና (AfCFTA) ጥሩ ምሳሌ ነው።
3. ASEAN (የደቡብ ምስራቅ እስያ)፦ በ1967 ሲመሰረት ዋና አላማቸው ከኮሚኒዝም ስርጭት ራስን መጠበቅ (Security) እንጂ ኢኮኖሚ አልነበረም። ነገር ግን በ1997 ከነበረው የኢኮኖሚ ቀውስ በኋላ ወደ ኢኮኖሚ ውህደት አተኮሩ።

4.9. Regionalization versus Globalization and State

The way regionalization, globalization and the state interact have various forms based on the issues under consideration. For instance, interaction on issues of economics and security greatly differ. In the international economy, globalization and regionalization appear to be pushing states in different directions, but there is today no major impetus toward globalization in the security arena, perhaps with the exception of nuclear issues such as nonproliferation (Lake 1997). Hence, regionalization of security is not a universal trend like the formation of economic regions.

👉 ግሎባላይዜሽን (አለማቀፋዊነት) እና ሪጅናላይዜሽን (ቀጠናዊነት) በኢኮኖሚ እና በፀጥታ ጉዳዮች ላይ ያላቸው ተፅዕኖ የተለያየ ነው። በኢኮኖሚ በኩል ሁለቱም ሀገራትን ወደተለያየ አቅጣጫ ሊጎትቱ ይችላሉ። ነገር ግን በፀጥታ (Security) ጉዳይ ላይ እንደ ኢኮኖሚው አለም አቀፋዊ የሆነ ትልቅ ውህደት የለም (ከኑክሌር ስምምነቶች ውጪ)። የፀጥታ ጉዳይ አሁንም በዋናነት በሀገራት ወይም በትንንሽ ቀጠናዎች እጅ ነው ያለው።

4.10. The Relations between Regionalization and Globalization

There are three possible options regarding the mutual relations between regionalization and globalization, especially in the economic dimension:

  • 1. Regionalization as a Component of Globalization (Convergence): Regionalism is understood as one component or 'chapter' of globalization. By helping national economies become more competitive, regional integration leads to multilateral cooperation on a global scale. Globalization unfolds in uneven dynamic patterns, expressed through regionalization.
  • 2. Regionalization as a Challenge or Response to Globalization (Divergence): Regionalism acts as a reaction and challenge to the amorphous, undemocratic, and inexorable economic rules of globalization. This reaction can be mercantilistic (opposing neoliberal 'harmony of interest' to favor national/regional loyalties) or pluralistic/humanistic (denial of a single universal culture).
  • 3. Regionalization and Globalization as Parallel Processes (Overlap): The world economy encompasses the trends of both regionalization (division into mega-regions like North America, Europe, East Asia) and globalization. They might act as parallel or overlapping processes rather than reacting to each other.

👉 በቀጠናዊነት እና በአለም አቀፋዊነት መካከል 3 አይነት ግንኙነቶች አሉ፦
1. Convergence (አጋዥ/አንድ አካል መሆን)፦ ሪጅናላይዜሽን የግሎባላይዜሽን አንዱ አካል ወይም 'ምዕራፍ' ነው ይላል። ለምሳሌ ሀገራት በቅድሚያ በቀጠናቸው ሲተባበሩ (እንደ COMESA) ለአለም አቀፍ ገበያ ይበልጥ ተወዳዳሪ ይሆናሉ።
2. Divergence (ተቃራኒ/ተገዳዳሪ መሆን)፦ ሪጅናላይዜሽን የተፈጠረው የግሎባላይዜሽንን ኢ-ፍትሃዊነት እና የባህል ወረራ (Homogenization) ለመከላከል ነው ይላል። ሀገራት የራሳቸውን ጥቅም ለመጠበቅ (Mercantilism) ቀጠናዊ ብሎኮችን ይፈጥራሉ።
3. Overlap (ትይዩ/አብሮ መጓዝ)፦ ሁለቱም ሂደቶች እርስበርስ ሳይጋጩ ጎን ለጎን በትይዩ ይጓዛሉ። የዓለም ኢኮኖሚ በታላላቅ ቀጠናዎች (Mega-regions) እየተከፋፈለ በተመሳሳይ ደግሞ አለምአቀፋዊ እየሆነ ነው።

4.11. Regionalization, Globalization and the State

Bringing the forces of nationalism and the possible role(s) of the nation-state into the equation creates 7 possible linkages. Let's explore the key dynamics:

Nation-States and Nationalism as Rival Processes of Globalization (Divergent): Processes of disintegration, fragmentation, autarky, and localization diverge from globalization. The blossoming of statehood or resurgence of nationalism is a response to the alienating forces of the global market, bolstering legitimacy at the national level.

Globalization as a Force of Nationalism (Convergent): Through technological dissemination, globalization might actually promote nationalism and the formation of new states through a 'global revolution of rising expectations.' Paradoxically, while globalization undermines state sovereignty, technological changes improve material conditions for the resurgence of nationalistic trends, creating new strategies for the state.

Nation-States as Rival Forces of Regionalization: States might oppose regionalization to transcend power/authority in a supranational direction by setting limits to regional identity. They guard their domestic jurisdiction and exercise of sovereignty.

Regionalism as a Force of Nationalism: Regionalization might result from mercantilistic/nationalistic tendencies of member-states to pool and increase their national power resources, similar to 'old' security alliances to guarantee greater security.

Nation-States as Mediators: States are active players. The stronger the states, the more capable they are in coping with the intricacies of globalization. Conversely, weaker states are more 'penetrated' or exposed to vulnerabilities and shallow world culture. Nationalism and globalization are linked dialectically. One possible option for states to cope with globalization is by enhancing processes of regionalization, recreating a double logic: liberal at the intraregional level but protectionist toward rival regions.

👉 እዚህ ጋር ሀገር (State)፣ ግሎባላይዜሽን እና ሪጅናላይዜሽን እንዴት እንደሚፋጠጡ እናያለን።
• አንዳንድ ጊዜ ብሄረተኝነት (Nationalism) ግሎባላይዜሽንን ይቃወማል። ሀገራት ባህላችን እና ኢኮኖሚያችን እንዳይዋጥ ብለው በራሳቸው ይወሸቃሉ (Autarky)።
• በሚገርም ሁኔታ ግሎባላይዜሽን ራሱ ብሄረተኝነትን ሊያቀጣጥል ይችላል። ቴክኖሎጂ እና ሶሻል ሚዲያ ሰዎች ስለ ማንነታቸው የበለጠ እንዲያስቡ እና አዳዲስ ሀገራት እንዲፈጠሩ ምክንያት ይሆናል።
• ጠንካራ ሀገራት (Strong states) በግሎባላይዜሽን ማዕበል አይጠለፉም፤ ሚዛናቸውን ይጠብቃሉ (Mediators)። ደካማ ሀገራት ግን በቀላሉ ይዋጣሉ (Penetrated)። ምሳሌ፦ ኢትዮጵያ ቴሌኮምን እና ባንክን ሙሉ ለሙሉ ለውጭ ባለሀብት ክፍት አለማድረጓ፣ የግሎባላይዜሽንን ጫና ሀገራዊ ጥቅምን (Nationalism) በሚጠብቅ መልኩ ለመቆጣጠር (Double logic: Protectionist) የምታደርገው ጥረት ማሳያ ነው።
